steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Crush garlic with rosemary, salt, and pepper in a mortar and pestle to make a paste. If you don’t have a mortar and pestle, mince ingredients finely and mash with the flat side of a knife.

Pierce meat with a sharp knife in several places and press garlic paste into the openings. Rub pork loin with the remaining garlic mixture and olive oil. Set into a small roasting pan or oven-safe skillet.

Place pork loin into the preheated oven, turning and basting with pan liquids every 30 minutes. Cook until the pork is no longer pink in the center, 90 minutes to 2 hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C). Remove roast to a platter and keep warm.
Place pan onto the stove over medium-high heat and pour wine into it. Heat wine and stir to loosen browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 3 to 5 minutes.
Slice pork loin and serve with pan juices.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Pork Loin
raw_recipe.description: This tender pork loin, roasted with garlic and rosemary and basted with a white wine pan sauce, makes a flavorsome and impressive main dish.

review.reviewBody:
I've made this recipe twice so far, and I've made a couple of adjustments to it. The first time I made it, I made exactly like the directions stated. Although, I used a meat thermometer, because my loin was perfect in 1 1/2 hrs.

The second time I made this, I pureed 4 cloves of garlic, 1/2 of the rosemary, and enough olive oil to bind it together. I rubbed my pork loin w/ the paste, then put in a ziploc bag in the fridge for a few hours to marinate. YUM! I threw in some veggies with my loin (carrots, onions and celery) and poured about 1/4 cup of wine in the bottom of the pan. Roasted for about 1.5 hours covered, and everything was perfect! I scooped out the veggies, and then used a can of chicken stock and some cornstarch to make a gravy out of the pan drippings. I served with buttered herb rice and the roasted vegetables. BIG hit! 5 stars! Thanks!

This is a great tasting roast. I used a 2.8-pound pork loin top loin roast for this recipe. I used fresh rosemary from my garden instead of dried, and added just a little onion and olive oil to the paste rub. About 1/4 through the cooking process, I added a little chicken broth and a little wine to the bottom of the roast, and about 20 minutes later, I turned the roast. I cooked the roast for 1 and ½ hours total, covered it with foil for about 10 minutes, and it came out done but very moist. I recommend using a meat thermometer, cooking time really depends on the cut and size of your meat. I added more chicken broth and wine to the drippings in the pan, a touch of flour to thicken, and everything turned out delicious! I served this with asparagus risotto. Thank you, Kathleen, for sharing this recipe.

My whole family really enjoyed this recipe. The pork was very tender and the sauce was probably the best part besides the wonderful aroma while cooking. I too reduced the cooking time to 1 hour and fifteen minutes and I even had a little over three pounds of pork loin. I also put the garlic/rosemary rub on the meat early in the morning and let it sit covered in the fridge all day. I used very little olive oil, just enough in my mini food processor to hold the rosemary and garlic together, around 2 to 3 tablespoons. My other recommendation would be to double the amount of rosemary/garlic mixture, especially when using more than 2 pounds of meat. I served this along with roasted potatoes and sauteed green beans with almonds........yum!

Very moist & FULL of taste! Made it for my husband for valentines day! Here's some tips!

1.) Always use your meat thermometer, if your loin is not moist, you probably overcooked it, all ovens and bake times vary...you paid good money for your meat, so cook accordingly! If you buy a loin that is packaged as one, but opens into two, Seperate them & roast side bey side. Stick the thermometer in the largest lion. I always take mine out at 165 degrees.
2.) I used Sherry as my wine. I poured the sherry in the pan with my loin, and afterwards added a little chicken stock and cornstarch for EXCELLENT gravy!!!
3.) While you have out the Sherry, reduce some mushrooms in Sherry, YUM!

This is a recipe that is too tasteful and easy to pass up!!!!

I made this for Christmas dinner instead of the usual ham. It was a big hit, and while easy was very festive looking! I used fresh rosemary instead of dried, added some dried sage, olive oil and dry vermouth to the paste, and also took the advice of another cook here and marinated the meat for a few hours in the paste. I used a roasting rack in a pan and threw in some fingerling potatoes tossed in olive oil for the last half hour of cooking, removing the aluminum foil and upping the temp to 375. I removed the potatoes to the serving platter and deglazed the roasting pan with white wine, which I mixed into a roux with a little chicken stock, and I let the meat rest on a grooved cutting board for 10 min and used the accumulated juices in the gravy. To serve I sliced the roast onto a serving tray with the potatoes arranged around the meat, poured a little gravy over it, served the rest in a boat. A very elegant yet easy meal!! If you don't care about making the gravy it is really hassle free, but since the meat is resting anyway (and I also steamed some green beans during that time) you might as well. Looking forward to seeing how the leftovers hold up. NOTE: I don't have a meat thermometer; my roast was just over 3 lbs and I cooked it for a good 2 hours to be safe. Came out perfect. I plan to make this again -- we are cutting out carbs in the new year and this would be just fine without the potatoes, maybe with some brussels sprouts instead :-)

This is DELICIOUS! Followed the recipe to the dot, and then covered the pork with a layer of sliced onion. The gravy I made with a bit of corn starch to make it thicker and a dash of herbes de provence because the wine I used was really strong. Served it with mashed potatoes and sauté buttered carrots and chopped onions. Hubby said it was restaurant quality and I loved it! Almost finished it all by myself.

I enjoyed this recipe. As is I would say it’s 3 1/2 stars but I’m rounding up for my rating above. It did need more flavor so I adjusted the seasonings. Also, instead of just using garlic paste, I used homemade garlic confit and it elevated the flavor. I also didn’t want the roast to dry out so after I seared it in a cast iron skillet, I put it in a 300 degree oven. It came out tender and juicy. Make sure you don’t skip the basting every 30 minutes!

The rub is a get flavor but the cooking time and method in this recipe will result in a very overdone pork loin. I usually wrap my pork lion tightly to hold in moisture then open and baste a couple of times at the tail end of the cooking even though recipes call for cooking uncovered because I just get better results (moist and tender). A pork loin of approx 2 lb’s would be done in less than an hour. I would recommend checking the temperature and basting at round 35-40 mins to get an idea of how far along you are the again every 5-10 mins or so depending on the temperature reading you got.

I tried the super simple recipe with great results! the aromatics smell While it was baking was incredible. I used a remote cooking thermometer And set it to the recommended 145 degrees. The timer went off right at 57 minutes. My roast was 2.2 lbs. served with small potatoes that I roasted along with it and a side of asparagus. Delicious!

I cooked this loin in a roaster oven with vegetables. I placed baby carrots (about a pound), chopped potatoes (about 2 pounds), 2 chopped onions, and a couple of chopped garlic cloves tossed with olive oil on the bottom of the roaster and then placed the pork with the rub on top. I had to cook the pork loin 70 minutes, perhaps it took longer because of the extra ingredients, but I used to meat thermometer to check for doneness. I removed everything from the roaster when the meat was at the proper temperature and then made the sauce according to the recipe. The meat came out tender and with a deliciously savory rub, and the vegetables were a wonderful accompaniment. I reheated the meat three times for subsequent meals and it still was tender and savory.

"I pureed 4 cloves of garlic, 1/2 of the rosemary, and enough olive oil to bind it together. I rubbed my pork loin w/ the paste, then put in a ziploc bag in the fridge for a few hours to marinate. YUM"

Roasted in Ninj after searing cooked to 145° ( you need a little more) because center was pink. Used chicken broth about 1/4 cup for moisture. Made gravy by adding another 1/4 cup of broth and let it cook down. Very moist!!
I used mustard as a binder instead of olive oil, and didn't have white wine. It was amazing though
Very easy delicious meal
Loved this recipe. I added a touch of Dijon mustard to the pan sauce. I think mustard goes really well with the fattiness of pork.

I used slabs of pork tenderloin, so I rubbed this garlic/EVOO/ fresh rosemary /S/P paste on and in slats then roasted it in air fryer to 145 F and it was wonderful. It took a fraction of the time and it was great for a single serving meal.

I use dijon mustard & spices on roast; sides: apples sauté in butter w/cinnamon & apple brandy, top w:havarti cheese, yam w/brown sugar, butter & nutmeg, brown gravy with pork drippings & mushrooms... peas w/pearl onions (need some green on plate)
You better really like rosemary for this recipe. Very strong.
I made this recipe with a 5 lb centercut pork loin reached 199F at 90 minutes perfect and it as juicy the wine sauce is a nice touch.Danny R
Might tweak ingridients next time but as is was very good, simple to make and tasty. Definitely recommended
